title: Five Below practice deep dive #3 (first US filer, specialty value retailer) - method test, NO verdict
body: PRACTICE run of the deep-dive protocol on a US filer, done to adapt the protocol to SEC filings (L9). There is no buy/sell/watchlist verdict and none should be inferred. Research, not advice. Key findings from filings: (1) Store model. The 10-K says 9,500 sq ft, ~$2M first-full-year sales, ~$0.4M cash investment (net of tenant allowances AND of payables, incl. pre-opening), payback ~1 year. The numerator is undefined and the text is unchanged from FY24 to FY25. Capex guidance ($100M for ~150 net new stores, gross of tenant allowances) implies ~$0.65M gross build-out per store. Reconciling it needs implausible tenant allowances of ~$0.48M, so the true cash investment is likely $0.6-0.7M and the payback ~1.6-1.9 years [EST]. Ship-centre capex (~$270M for 5 DCs, ~$0.14M per store) sits outside the model. A rebuilt four-wall EBITDA is ~23% (mature, $2.5M) and ~18-19% (new, $2.0M) [EST, two routes agree]. (2) Tariffs. A $163.6M IEEPA tariff refund was credited to Q2 FY26 COGS (13% of the quarter's sales): GAAP EPS $3.99 vs adjusted $1.68; FY26 GAAP EPS guide $12.10-12.58 vs adjusted $9.83-10.31. That implies an effective IEEPA rate of ~20-22% on direct-import FOB (~40% of purchases are direct imports; 60% come from domestic vendors, whose embedded tariffs are not refundable to FIVE). (3) Occupancy. FY25 new leases: 141 leases, $258.0M of minimum payments, ~$183k a year (~$19/sq ft base). Net lease cost $449.9M = 9.4% of sales. Lease liabilities $2.03B vs $0.93B cash and investments, no funded debt. (4) Labour. ~23,000 store crew = ~12 per store (both years). Payroll is not disclosed; estimated at 13.6-16.8% of sales; 1% wage ≈ 15 bps; $1/hour ≈ 90-110 bps [EST]. (5) SBC $34.7M (0.73% of sales), shares flat for 10 years via ~$34M a year of buybacks; $600M authorisation Aug-2026. (6) Management. New CEO (Dec-2024), CFO (Oct-2025) and CMO; founder left the board in Jun-2025; class action in discovery. (7) Promises. The 2022 investor-day 'Triple-Double' was 65-84% delivered by FY25, and the 10-K softened '3,500 by 2030' to 'over time'. Near-term comp guides were beaten 5 of 5 times by 4.4-8.4 pp. (8) Insiders sold $13.3M (7 insiders, 25 transactions; 5-insider cluster after the Q2 print); the CEO did not sell; 1 small director buy. 13G: Vanguard 0% is a reporting realignment, not a sale; T. Rowe IM exited 6.6% to 0% in 2025; BlackRock 4.90M to 5.50M shares. Open soft flags: 6, so no position without a written variant view.

dated_watch: DEF 14A PSU metric treatment of tariff refunds

title: Triangulate a retailer's headline 'new store investment/payback' against its own capex-per-new-store guidance
body: Company store models (e.g. '$0.4M investment, ~1-year payback') are targets with undefined numerators. They are often net of tenant allowances and payables, and they exclude network capex (DCs, systems). Divide the 10-K/MD&A capex budgeted for new stores by planned gross openings, then rebuild: build-out − tenant allowance + inventory net of payables + pre-opening (from the pre-opening note). If reconciling needs a tenant allowance above ~40% of build-out, treat the headline as stale or narrowly defined and recompute the payback. Add DC capex ÷ stores served. Five Below FY26: $100M / ~155 openings ≈ $0.65M gross vs '$0.4M'; implied payback ~1.6-1.9 years, not ~1. Also diff the store-model paragraph year over year: unchanged numbers through cost inflation are a flag.

title: A tariff refund booked in COGS reveals the tariff cost actually borne; split importer-of-record from domestic-vendor exposure
body: After the Feb-2026 Supreme Court IEEPA ruling, US importers booked refunds, usually as a COGS credit, and stripped them out of adjusted numbers. (1) The refund ÷ direct-import FOB (purchases × import share ÷ (1 + rate)) gives the effective tariff rate borne. Five Below: $163.6M on ~40% direct imports ≈ 20-22% effective. (2) GAAP EPS and GAAP gross margin are distorted for four quarters (FIVE Q2 FY26 GAAP GM 48.5% vs adjusted 35.6%), so screens on trailing GAAP numbers mislead. (3) Goods bought from domestic vendors carried tariffs inside the vendor price. Those refunds go to the vendor, not the retailer. Ask whether vendors pass any back. Nobody asked this on the call. (4) Check how the proxy's PSU metric treats the refund.

title: Promise tracker: score long-range (investor-day) and near-term (quarterly guide) promises separately, and by management team
body: Five Below shows the two can diverge completely. The 2022 'Triple-Double' investor-day targets (prior CEO) were 65-84% delivered by FY25, and the 3,500-stores-by-2030 target was silently softened to 'over time' in the 10-K. Yet the new CEO/CFO beat quarterly comp guidance 5 of 5 times, by 4.4-8.4 pp. A single blended credibility score would mislead both ways. Also compute the implied remaining-quarter figure from any full-year guide (FIVE FY26 10-12% comps ⇒ Q4 ≈ +3%) before setting a paper-call probability. Diff the 10-K wording each year (deleted dates and qualifiers are cheap signals).

title: US ownership filings: read 13G remarks and Form 4 codes before inferring buying or selling
body: (1) Vanguard's 13G/As filed after its 12-Jan-2026 internal realignment show 0% beneficial ownership with no sale (disaggregated reporting); the 13F still shows the shares. (2) 13F is long-only with a 45-day lag; compare share counts, not values (our tool misparsed T. Rowe's value units). (3) Form 4: only P/S are open-market; A/M/F/G are grants, exercises, tax withholding and gifts; confirm the 10b5-1 checkbox on the form. Insider sale clusters after a rally or vesting window are weak evidence (L14: even buy clusters showed ~0 excess vs matched controls). FIVE Mar-Nov 2026: $13.3M of sales by 7 insiders, CEO none; this is recorded as an open-low flag only.
